chunks: Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Miskan, from Zurara who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): May Allah set you aright, the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic in His book: "The Fitra of Allah which He created the people upon"
He (the Imam) said: He created them upon Tawhid, at the Covenant, upon His Ma'rifa (Recognition) that He is their Lord.
I said: Did they address Him?
He (Zurara) said: so he (the Imam) lowered his head and then said: If it were not for that they would not know who their Lord is nor who their Sustainer is.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Fitra in the context of the Primordial Covenant according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from the school of Zurara, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'Fitra' mentioned in Surah Ar-Rum is not merely a general disposition but the specific, pre-temporal recognition of Tawhid established during the Mithaq (Primordial Covenant). The Imam’s gesture and subsequent remark emphasize that without this innate, divinely implanted knowledge, humanity would lack the fundamental capacity to identify their Lord and Sustainer, linking the metaphysical origin of the soul to its epistemological certainty.

en.ammaar-muslim: 7. [7/384] al-Tawhid: My father from Sa’d from Ahmad b. Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughira from Ibn Muskan from Zurara who said:
I said to Abi Ja’far عليه السلام: May Allah set you aright, the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic in His book: “The Fitra of Allah which He created the people upon” [30:30]?
He (the Imam) said: He created them upon Tawhid, at the Covenant, upon His Ma’rifa (Recognition) that He is their Lord.
I said: Did they address Him?
He (Zurara) said: so he (the Imam) lowered his head and then said: If it were not for that they would not know who their Lord is nor who their Sustainer is.
